name: Test

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

permissions: {}

# Enrich gradle.properties for CI/CD
env:
  GRADLE_OPTS: -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx6g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError" -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options=-Xmx2g -XX:+UseG1GC
  CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES: --stacktrace --no-configuration-cache

jobs:
  tests:
    name: Runs unit tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Allow all jobs on main. Just one per PR.
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && format('unit-tests-main-{0}', github.sha) || format('unit-tests-{0}', github.ref) }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - name: ⏬ Checkout with LFS
        uses: nschloe/action-cached-lfs-checkout@385a8ecc719e50b8c71af6ab01a624b486b7c3bc # v1.2.5
        with:
          # Ensure we are building the branch and not the branch after being merged on main
          # https://github.com/actions/checkout/issues/881
          ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Fetch the matrix-rust-rtc AAR
        # The core is not on Maven Central yet: gradle.properties pins its release asset and sha256,
        # and the script fetches it into rtc/local (docs/local_stack.md, layer 1).
        run: ./tools/rtc/fetch-rust-rtc
      - name: ☕️ Use JDK 21
        uses: actions/setup-java@dd06d9cba3e5552c54d9f8ea23572deb30010f7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '21'
      - name: Configure gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@9c971963bec38e04b3d30dcc455b5382be2fdbfb # v6.3.0
        with:
          cache-read-only: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: ⚙️ Run unit tests
        run: ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest -x :tests:konsist:testDebugUnitTest $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES

      - name: ⚙️ Run screenshot tests
        # Compares against the PNGs committed in tests/uitests/src/test/snapshots (Git LFS). Recording is
        # done by the "Record screenshots" workflow, never locally. See docs/screenshot_testing.md.
        run: ./gradlew :tests:uitests:verifyPaparazziDebug $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES

      - name: ⚙️ Generate kover coverage report
        run: ./gradlew :koverXmlReportMerged :koverHtmlReportMerged :koverVerifyAll -x testDebugUnitTest $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES

      - name: 🚫 Upload kover failed coverage reports
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: kover-error-report
          path: |
            build/reports/kover

      - name: 🚫 Upload test results on error
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: tests-results
          path: |
            **/build/paparazzi/failures/
            **/build/reports/tests/*UnitTest/

# Screenshot testing

<!--- TOC -->

* [Overview](#overview)
* [Setup](#setup)
* [Recording](#recording)
* [Verifying](#verifying)
* [Contributing](#contributing)

<!--- END -->

## Overview

- Screenshot tests record the content of a rendered composable and verify subsequent runs to check if it renders
  differently.
- This library uses [Paparazzi](https://github.com/cashapp/paparazzi) to render, record and verify composables, the
  way Element X Android does. Every `internal` composable annotated `@PreviewsDayNight` in `call/ui` is a
  screenshot test, thanks to [ComposablePreviewScanner](https://github.com/sergio-sastre/ComposablePreviewScanner):
  one day and one night PNG per preview, one per value of its `PreviewParameterProvider`.
- The tests live in `tests/uitests`, a module of its own so that Paparazzi and layoutlib stay off the published
  modules and the PNGs out of their source trees. They render with the default `ElementCallStyle`; a host's own
  style is its own screenshot suite's business.
- The screenshot verification occurs on every pull request as part of the `tests.yml` workflow.

## Setup

- Install Git LFS through your package manager of choice (`brew install git-lfs` | `yay -S git-lfs`).
- Install the Git LFS hooks into the project.

```shell
# with element-call-android as the current working directory
git lfs install --local
```

If installed correctly, `git push` and `git pull` will now include LFS content.

## Recording

Recording is done by the GitHub action "Record screenshots" (`.github/workflows/recordScreenshots.yml`), to avoid
differences in the generated PNGs between developers' machines. Either add the `Record-Screenshots` label to the
pull request, or run the workflow by hand on a branch. The action records, commits `Update screenshots` to the
branch and removes the label. The workflow fetches the pinned RTC AAR with `tools/rtc/fetch-rust-rtc`, like every
other one: the previews render `call/ui`, which links the RTC AAR for its video renderer.

You can still record locally to look at the result, but do not commit what it produces:

```shell
./gradlew recordPaparazziDebug
```

The task deletes `tests/uitests/src/test/snapshots` before recording (the `removeOldSnapshots` task in the root
build file). The images land in the same folder, and are committed to the repository through Git LFS.

## Verifying

```shell
./gradlew verifyPaparazziDebug
```

In the case of failure, Paparazzi writes images to `tests/uitests/build/paparazzi/failures`: the expected and
actual screenshots along with a delta of the two.

## Contributing

- Every main state of a public composable has a preview (`AGENTS.md`, "Previews and screenshots"), so a new state
  is a new screenshot for free.
- After adding or changing a preview, have the screenshots recorded (label or workflow) before asking for review.
- `./tools/git/validate_lfs.sh` checks that every PNG went through Git LFS; the CI runs it too.

name: Record screenshots

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    types: [ labeled ]

permissions: {}

# Enrich gradle.properties for CI/CD
env:
  GRADLE_OPTS: -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx8g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:+UseG1GC -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options=-Xmx4g
  CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES: --no-configuration-cache

jobs:
  record:
    permissions:
      # Need write permissions on PRs to remove the label "Record-Screenshots"
      pull-requests: write
      contents: write
    # This job runs the pull request's own Gradle build with the write token above. That is safe only under
    # `pull_request`, where GitHub hands a fork a read-only token whatever is declared here: never switch it to
    # `pull_request_target`, which would run a stranger's build script with write access to this repository.
    name: Record screenshots on branch ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref || github.ref_name }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.label.name == 'Record-Screenshots'

    steps:
      - name: Remove Record-Screenshots label
        if: github.event.label.name == 'Record-Screenshots'
        uses: actions-ecosystem/action-remove-labels@2ce5d41b4b6aa8503e285553f75ed56e0a40bae0 # v1.3.0
        with:
          labels: Record-Screenshots
      - name: ⏬ Checkout with LFS (PR)
        if: github.event.label.name == 'Record-Screenshots'
        uses: nschloe/action-cached-lfs-checkout@385a8ecc719e50b8c71af6ab01a624b486b7c3bc # v1.2.5
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.ref || github.ref }}
      - name: ⏬ Checkout with LFS (Branch)
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        uses: nschloe/action-cached-lfs-checkout@385a8ecc719e50b8c71af6ab01a624b486b7c3bc # v1.2.5
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Fetch the matrix-rust-rtc AAR
        # The core is not on Maven Central yet: gradle.properties pins its release asset and sha256,
        # and the script fetches it into rtc/local (docs/local_stack.md, layer 1).
        run: ./tools/rtc/fetch-rust-rtc
      - name: ☕️ Use JDK 21
        uses: actions/setup-java@dd06d9cba3e5552c54d9f8ea23572deb30010f7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '21'
      - name: Configure gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@9c971963bec38e04b3d30dcc455b5382be2fdbfb # v6.3.0
        with:
          cache-read-only: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - name: Record screenshots
        id: record
        run: ./.github/workflows/scripts/recordScreenshots.sh
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          GRADLE_ARGS: ${{ env.CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES }}

name: Instrumented tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

permissions: {}

# Enrich gradle.properties for CI/CD
env:
  GRADLE_OPTS: -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx6g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError" -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options=-Xmx2g -XX:+UseG1GC
  CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES: --stacktrace --no-configuration-cache

jobs:
  emulator:
    name: Sample app on an emulator
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Allow all jobs on main. Just one per PR.
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && format('instrumented-main-{0}', github.sha) || format('instrumented-{0}', github.ref) }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Fetch the matrix-rust-rtc AAR
        # The core is not on Maven Central yet: gradle.properties pins its release asset and sha256,
        # and the script fetches it into rtc/local (docs/local_stack.md, layer 1). The AAR ships x86_64, which is
        # what the emulator below runs.
        run: ./tools/rtc/fetch-rust-rtc
      - name: Enable KVM
        # Hardware acceleration for the emulator on the hosted runners.
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      - name: ☕️ Use JDK 21
        uses: actions/setup-java@dd06d9cba3e5552c54d9f8ea23572deb30010f7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '21'
      - name: Configure gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@9c971963bec38e04b3d30dcc455b5382be2fdbfb # v6.3.0
        with:
          cache-read-only: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - name: Run the sample's instrumented tests
        # The floating tile's drag, the strip's paging and a tile's pixels: what only a touch pipeline
        # and a GL surface can answer for (plan §7.2).
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@a421e43855164a8197daf9d8d40fe71c6996bb0d # v2.38.0
        with:
          api-level: 34
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          profile: pixel_6
          disable-animations: true
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim -camera-back none
          script: ./gradlew :sample:connectedDebugAndroidTest $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES
      - name: 🚫 Upload test results on error
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: instrumented-tests-results
          path: |
            sample/build/reports/androidTests/
            sample/build/outputs/androidTest-results/

name: Consumer check

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

permissions: {}

# Enrich gradle.properties for CI/CD
env:
  GRADLE_OPTS: -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx6g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=1g -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError" -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options=-Xmx2g -XX:+UseG1GC
  CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES: --stacktrace --no-configuration-cache

jobs:
  consumer:
    name: Publish locally and build a minified consumer
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Allow all jobs on main. Just one per PR.
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && format('consumer-main-{0}', github.sha) || format('consumer-{0}', github.ref) }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Fetch the matrix-rust-rtc AAR
        # The core is not on Maven Central yet: gradle.properties pins its release asset and sha256,
        # and the script fetches it into rtc/local (docs/local_stack.md, layer 1).
        run: ./tools/rtc/fetch-rust-rtc
      - name: ☕️ Use JDK 21
        uses: actions/setup-java@dd06d9cba3e5552c54d9f8ea23572deb30010f7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '21'
      - name: Configure gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@9c971963bec38e04b3d30dcc455b5382be2fdbfb # v6.3.0
        with:
          cache-read-only: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - name: Publish the artifacts to the local Maven repository
        # The published shape - POMs, module metadata, consumer rules, manifests - is what the next step
        # consumes, and what the composite build in Element X never sees (plan §8.4).
        run: ./gradlew publishToMavenLocal -PVERSION_NAME=0.0.0-ci $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES
      - name: Build the minified consumer against them
        run: ./gradlew -p tests/consumer :app:assembleRelease -PelementCallVersion=0.0.0-ci $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES
      - name: Upload the consumer APK
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: consumer-release-apk
          path: tests/consumer/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk

name: Code Quality Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

permissions: {}

# Enrich gradle.properties for CI/CD
env:
  GRADLE_OPTS: -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx6g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:+UseG1GC -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options=-Xmx3g
  CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES: --stacktrace --no-daemon --no-configuration-cache

jobs:
  checkScript:
    name: Search for forbidden patterns
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Refuse a tracked AAR or a committed local-stack property
        run: |
          if git ls-files | grep -q '\.aar$'; then
            echo "::error::A .aar file is tracked by git. The matrix-rust-rtc AAR is a local file, see docs/local_stack.md."
            exit 1
          fi
          if git grep -n -E 'elementCallAndroidDir|elementCallLocalVersion' -- '*.properties' '*.gradle.kts'; then
            echo "::error::A local-stack property is committed, see docs/local_stack.md."
            exit 1
          fi

  quality:
    name: Konsist, lint, detekt, ktlint, ABI and docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Allow all jobs on main. Just one per PR.
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && format('quality-main-{0}', github.sha) || format('quality-{0}', github.ref) }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Ensure we are building the branch and not the branch after being merged on main
          # https://github.com/actions/checkout/issues/881
          ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Fetch the matrix-rust-rtc AAR
        # The core is not on Maven Central yet: gradle.properties pins its release asset and sha256,
        # and the script fetches it into rtc/local (docs/local_stack.md, layer 1).
        run: ./tools/rtc/fetch-rust-rtc
      - name: Use JDK 21
        uses: actions/setup-java@dd06d9cba3e5552c54d9f8ea23572deb30010f7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '21'
      - name: Configure gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@9c971963bec38e04b3d30dcc455b5382be2fdbfb # v6.3.0
        with:
          cache-read-only: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - name: Run quality checks
        run: ./gradlew runQualityChecks $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES
      - name: Upload reports on error
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: quality-reports
          path: |
            **/build/reports/lint-results-*.html
            **/build/reports/detekt/
            **/build/reports/ktlint/
            **/build/reports/tests/*UnitTest/

name: Release

# Cuts a release from a release/<version> branch, the way element-call-ios does: scripts/release.sh
# validates the version, generates the notes from the pull request labels, closes the changelog section,
# stamps VERSION_NAME, builds and tests, and lays out the release assets; this workflow then drafts the GitHub
# release with the assets, commits, tags v<version>, pushes both atomically and publishes the release, which is
# where a host resolves the library from (README, "Consuming a release"). The changelog reaches main afterwards
# through an ordinary pull request. See RELEASING.md, including why publishing to Maven Central is gated on a
# repository variable.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release, bare semver: 0.1.0, or 0.2.0-rc.1 for a prerelease (the tag gets the v)"
        required: true
      dry_run:
        description: "Validate, build and print, change nothing"
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions: {}

# Never two at once, and never cancel one in flight: between the push and the release there is a moment
# where the tag exists and the release does not, and cancelling there leaves that visible.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GRADLE_OPTS: -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx6g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=1g -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError" -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options=-Xmx2g -XX:+UseG1GC
  CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES: --stacktrace --no-configuration-cache

jobs:
  release:
    name: Release ${{ inputs.version }}${{ inputs.dry_run && ' (dry run)' || '' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60

    # Skip in forks
    if: github.repository == 'element-hq/element-call-android'

    # GITHUB_TOKEN is enough, and that is the point of releasing from a branch rather than from main. The
    # release commit and tag go to release/<version>, which is not protected, so nothing here needs a
    # personal access token that can bypass protection on main; the changelog reaches main afterwards
    # through an ordinary reviewed pull request. contents:write for the branch, the tag and the release.
    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      # The full history and all tags, because the script reads the tags reachable from HEAD to decide both
      # what the previous release was and whether this version goes backwards. Credentials persist because
      # the push below is this same checkout's; every other workflow drops them.
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: true

      # A dry run is a read; rehearse it from anywhere, including main. Publishing must come from
      # release/<version>, and the branch name must agree with the version being released, so a run
      # dispatched against the wrong branch cannot mint a tag off it.
      - name: Check the branch
        env:
          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
        run: |
          if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Dry run on $BRANCH."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "$BRANCH" != "release/$VERSION" ]; then
            echo "::error::To release $VERSION, dispatch this from a branch named release/$VERSION (this is $BRANCH). See RELEASING.md."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Releasing $VERSION from $BRANCH."

      - name: Fetch the matrix-rust-rtc AAR
        # The core is not on Maven Central yet: gradle.properties pins its release asset and sha256,
        # and the script fetches it into rtc/local (docs/local_stack.md, layer 1).
        run: ./tools/rtc/fetch-rust-rtc
      - name: ☕️ Use JDK 21
        uses: actions/setup-java@dd06d9cba3e5552c54d9f8ea23572deb30010f7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '21'
      - name: Configure gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@9c971963bec38e04b3d30dcc455b5382be2fdbfb # v6.3.0
        with:
          cache-read-only: true

      # Validates the version, generates the notes from the pull request labels, prepends them to CHANGES.md,
      # stamps VERSION_NAME, then builds, tests, checks, publishes locally, builds the minified consumer twice
      # and lays out the release assets. Touches nothing but the working tree, build/ and ~/.m2, so it is the
      # same command a maintainer runs to rehearse. Every refusal is in there.
      - name: Prepare the release
        id: prepare
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          DRY_RUN_FLAG: ${{ inputs.dry_run && '--dry-run' || '' }}
        # $DRY_RUN_FLAG unquoted on purpose: it must vanish when empty rather than become an empty
        # argument. It is a literal chosen by the expression above, never user input.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        run: ./scripts/release.sh "$VERSION" $DRY_RUN_FLAG

      # The two files the release commit will carry, shown while a dry run is the only chance to read them
      # before the tag exists.
      - name: Show the release diff
        run: git --no-pager diff -- CHANGES.md gradle.properties

      - name: Build the sample APK
        run: ./gradlew :sample:assembleDebug $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES

      # Uploaded on every run, before anything is published. On a dry run this is the output to read; on a
      # real run it is the recovery path: if drafting or publishing the release fails, the notes and assets it
      # needed are here, and RELEASING.md's "If it fails halfway" says what to do with them.
      - name: Upload the notes, changelog and assets
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-${{ inputs.version }}${{ inputs.dry_run && '-dry-run' || '' }}
          path: |
            ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.notes }}
            CHANGES.md
            gradle.properties
            build/release-assets/
            sample/build/outputs/apk/debug/sample-debug.apk
          retention-days: 30
          if-no-files-found: error

      # Everything from here changes the world, so the dry run stops here. dry_run defaults to true: the
      # normal path is to run this workflow twice.

      # Releases are immutable: assets can be added only to a draft, so the release is drafted with all of them
      # here, before the tag is pushed, and published once it is. A failed upload leaves a draft and no tag, and
      # dispatching again finishes the draft. --clobber only ever replaces an asset of a draft, which nobody can
      # have resolved yet. The assets are what a host's Ivy repository resolves, so their names are the
      # artifacts' own (<artifactId>-<version>[-classifier].<ext>) and must not change.
      - name: Draft the release
        if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          PRERELEASE: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.prerelease }}
          NOTES: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.notes }}
        run: |
          assets=(build/release-assets/* sample/build/outputs/apk/debug/sample-debug.apk)
          draft="$(gh release view "$TAG" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo none)"
          case "$draft" in
            none)
              args=(--draft --title "$TAG" --notes-file "$NOTES")
              if [ "$PRERELEASE" = "yes" ]; then
                args+=(--prerelease)
              fi
              gh release create "$TAG" "${args[@]}" "${assets[@]}"
              ;;
            true)
              echo "Release $TAG is already drafted; finishing its assets."
              gh release upload "$TAG" "${assets[@]}" --clobber
              ;;
            *)
              echo "Release $TAG is already published; leaving it alone."
              ;;
          esac

      # One --atomic push, so the tag and the changelog entry describing it land together or not at all, and
      # the tagged tree contains its own changelog and its own version. Path-explicit add, not `git add -A`:
      # a new generated file has to be named here or it never reaches the tag.
      - name: Commit, tag and push
        if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run }}
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.version }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "ElementBot"
          git config user.email "android@element.io"
          git add CHANGES.md gradle.properties
          git commit -m "Release $VERSION"
          git tag -a "$TAG" -m "$TAG"
          git push --atomic origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$BRANCH" "refs/tags/$TAG"

      # Idempotent, because the tag is pushed in the step above and re-dispatching the same version would be
      # refused for existing already. If this step is what failed, running the workflow again cannot be the
      # fix, so it must be able to finish the job on a release that is already published.
      #
      # --verify-tag so it refuses to publish a release whose tag the push above did not land. Publishing
      # makes it immutable: its assets and its tag never change again.
      - name: Publish the release
        if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          if [ "$(gh release view "$TAG" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)" = "true" ]; then
            gh release edit "$TAG" --draft=false --verify-tag
          else
            echo "Release $TAG is already published; leaving it alone."
          fi
          gh release view "$TAG" --json url,isPrerelease,tagName,assets --jq '{url, isPrerelease, tagName, assets: [.assets[].name]}'

      - name: Publish to Maven Central
        # Gated: a Central release is immutable and public. Set MAVEN_CENTRAL_PUBLISH=true once the
        # prerequisites in RELEASING.md are met (a Central Portal account for io.element.android, the
        # signing key, and the core on Central).
        if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run && vars.MAVEN_CENTRAL_PUBLISH == 'true' }}
        env:
          ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_mavenCentralUsername: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_mavenCentralPassword: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_signingInMemoryKey: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_SIGNING_KEY }}
          ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_signingInMemoryKeyPassword: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: ./gradlew publishAndReleaseToMavenCentral -PRELEASE_SIGNING_ENABLED=true $CI_GRADLE_ARG_PROPERTIES

      # The tag is the release and it is already public; this pull request only carries the changelog entry
      # and the version back to main. Opened by hand, deliberately: a pull request opened with GITHUB_TOKEN
      # does not trigger other workflows, so the checks would not run on it.
      - name: Say what is left to do
        if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run }}
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          REPO_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Released $TAG"
            echo
            echo "- Tag and release: [$TAG]($REPO_URL/releases/tag/$TAG)"
            echo
            echo "**Now open the pull request** that carries the changelog entry and VERSION_NAME back to \`main\`:"
            echo
            echo "  $REPO_URL/compare/main...$BRANCH?expand=1"
            echo
            echo "Merge it with a **merge commit**, not a squash, so the tagged commit stays an ancestor of \`main\`. See RELEASING.md."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Pull Request Label

# The release notes are built from exactly one pr- label per pull request (.github/release.yml, RELEASING.md).
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [ opened, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, synchronize ]
  merge_group:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  label:
    name: Require one pr- label
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Skipped in the merge queue, which counts as passing: the label was checked on the pull request.
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |
            .github/release.yml
            .github/workflows/scripts/checkPrLabel.sh
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
      - name: Check the pr- label
        env:
          LABELS: ${{ toJSON(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name) }}
        run: ./.github/workflows/scripts/checkPrLabel.sh

package io.element.android.call.api.rtc

/**
 * What is interrupting the call now, cause by cause (feature-hq 034 C5). The core names no entry and no text: grouping is the
 * UI's. Member lists hold member ids on the roster; [unmappable] holds transport identities that map to no member.
 */
data class MatrixRtcInterruptions(
    val signalling: MatrixRtcSignallingHealth,
    val isOwnMembershipLapsed: Boolean,
    /** Authoritative for our own SFU from the first value, before our own tile exists. */
    val ownMedia: MatrixRtcConnectionState,
    val membersReconnecting: List<String>,
    val membersUnreachable: List<String>,
    val unableToDecrypt: List<String>,
    val unmappable: List<String>,
) {
    companion object {
        val NONE = MatrixRtcInterruptions(
            signalling = MatrixRtcSignallingHealth.Reachable,
            isOwnMembershipLapsed = false,
            ownMedia = MatrixRtcConnectionState.CONNECTED,
            membersReconnecting = emptyList(),
            membersUnreachable = emptyList(),
            unableToDecrypt = emptyList(),
            unmappable = emptyList(),
        )
    }
}

#!/bin/bash

# Copyright (c) 2026 Element Creations Ltd.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Element-Commercial.
# Please see LICENSE files in the repository root for full details.

# Fails unless $LABELS, the pull request's labels as a JSON array, holds exactly one pr- label that
# .github/release.yml knows.

set -euo pipefail

ALLOWED=$(grep -oE '^[[:space:]]*- pr-[a-z]+' .github/release.yml | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*- //')
FOUND=$(jq -r '.[] | select(startswith("pr-"))' <<<"${LABELS:-[]}")
COUNT=$(grep -c . <<<"$FOUND" || true)

if [ "$COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::Add exactly one pr- label from .github/release.yml: $(echo $ALLOWED)"
    exit 1
fi
if [ "$COUNT" -gt 1 ]; then
    echo "::error::Keep exactly one pr- label, found: $(echo $FOUND)"
    exit 1
fi
if ! grep -qxF "$FOUND" <<<"$ALLOWED"; then
    echo "::error::$FOUND is not in .github/release.yml, use one of: $(echo $ALLOWED)"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Release notes label: $FOUND"

#!/bin/bash

# Copyright (c) 2026 Element Creations Ltd.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Element-Commercial.
# Please see LICENSE files in the repository root for full details.

set -e

TOKEN=[REDACTED]
REPO=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY

SHORT=t:,r:
LONG=token:,repo:
OPTS=$(getopt -a -n recordScreenshots --options $SHORT --longoptions $LONG -- "$@")

eval set -- "$OPTS"
while :
do
  case "$1" in
    -t | --token )
      TOKEN="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    -r | --repo )
      REPO="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --)
      shift;
      break
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unexpected option: $1"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done

BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
echo Branch used: $BRANCH

if [[ -z ${TOKEN} ]]; then
  echo "No token specified, either set the env var GITHUB_TOKEN or use the --token option"
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -z ${REPO} ]]; then
  echo "No repo specified, either set the env var GITHUB_REPOSITORY or use the --repo option"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Deleting previous screenshots"
./gradlew removeOldSnapshots --stacktrace --warn $GRADLE_ARGS

echo "Record screenshots"
./gradlew recordPaparazziDebug --stacktrace $GRADLE_ARGS

echo "Committing changes"

if [[ -z ${INPUT_AUTHOR_NAME} ]]; then
  git config user.name "ElementBot"
else
  git config --local user.name "${INPUT_AUTHOR_NAME}"
fi

if [[ -z ${INPUT_AUTHOR_EMAIL} ]]; then
  git config user.email "android@element.io"
else
  git config --local user.email "${INPUT_AUTHOR_EMAIL}"
fi
git add -A
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "Screenshots are already up to date, nothing to commit."
  exit 0
fi
git commit -m "Update screenshots"

GITHUB_REPO="https://$GITHUB_ACTOR:$TOKEN@github.com/$REPO.git"
echo "Pushing changes"
if [[ -z ${GITHUB_ACTOR} ]]; then
  echo "No GITHUB_ACTOR env var"
  GITHUB_REPO="https://$TOKEN@github.com/$REPO.git"
fi
git push $GITHUB_REPO "$BRANCH"
echo "Done!"

import org.matrix.rustcomponents.sdk.EventEncryptionInfo
import org.matrix.rustcomponents.sdk.ShieldState

const val A_SENDER_DEVICE = "SENDERDEVICE"

fun anEncryptionInfo(senderId: String, shield: ShieldState) = EventEncryptionInfo(
    senderId = senderId,
    senderDeviceId = A_SENDER_DEVICE,
    senderCurve25519Key = "curve",
    sessionId = null,
    shieldState = shield,
    shieldStateStrict = shield,
)
